claim: On June 24, 2025, the Clay County BCC denied a land-use change (Agriculture to Rural Residential, ~13 dwelling units) requested by applicant Cheryl Gustafson for a 13.86-acre parcel off CR 16A in Green Cove Springs, by a 4-1 vote, against staff/Planning Commission/Springs CAC recommendations of approval.
documentName: Commissioners deny Gustafson land-use change for 13.86-acre Green Cove parcel — CitizenPortal.ai
extract: UPDATED 2026-09-11 — now cross-checked against the official BCC minutes (see EV-010). CONFIRMED accurate: date (June 24, 2025), 13.86-acre parcel off CR 16A/Green Cove Springs, AG-to-RR request, 4-1 denial vote, staff/Planning Commission/Springs CAC all recommending approval. CORRECTED: the applicant's first name is Sheryl, not Cheryl (see EV-010/EV-012). DISPROVEN: this article's claim that a 'Commissioner John Burke' opposed the change and a 'Commissioner Magdalen' made the motion to deny — see EV-011, which documents the real mover/seconder/dissenter from the primary minutes. CitizenPortal.ai is an AI-generated meeting-summary aggregator, not a primary record, and should not be relied on for attribution detail even when its topline facts check out.

claim: Official BCC minutes for June 24, 2025 confirm: applicant Sheryl Edlyn Gustafson requested COMP 25-0010 (FLUM AG→RR) and ZON 25-0007 (AG→AR) for a 13.86-acre parcel at 2005 S CR 16-A, Green Cove Springs (Parcel 16-06-26-015574-001-02, District 5/Comm. Burke), for up to 13 single-family lots. The Springs Citizen Advisory Committee (6-0, May 14, 2025) and Planning Commission (6-0, June 3, 2025) both recommended approval, and staff recommended approval of both applications. Vice-Chairman Kristen Burke made the motion to DENY COMP 25-0010, seconded by Commissioner John Sgromolo, which carried 4-1 with Commissioner Jim Renninger opposed to the denial. Because the comprehensive-plan amendment was denied, the companion rezoning (ZON 25-0007) was not considered. Chairman Betsy Condon recommended the applicant reapply with a minimum lot size or as a PUD.
documentName: Board of County Commissioners Meeting Minutes and Attachments, June 24, 2025 (Item 20) — e-signed by Clerk Tara S. Green and Commissioner Betsy Condon
extract: Directly fetched and read the official, e-signed BCC minutes PDF via Clay County's PrimeGov portal (meeting id 1833, Board of County Commissioners Meeting, committeeId 1). Danielle Kitchens, identified as the applicant's real estate agent, answered Board questions about the applicants' residence, intent to sell, and future plans. Discussion covered development options, lot sizes, selling price, minimum lot size, code compliance, water/sewer, and density before the vote. This is the single highest-confidence source in this investigation to date: a signed, dated, primary government document with an authenticated e-signature audit trail (Lisa Osha → Betsy Condon → Tara S. Green, completed 2025-07-14).

claim: CitizenPortal.ai's claim that a 'Commissioner John Burke' opposed the Gustafson request and a 'Commissioner Magdalen' moved to deny it is false; neither person exists on Clay County's BCC. The actual mover was Vice-Chairman Kristen Burke, the actual seconder was Commissioner John Sgromolo, and the actual dissenting vote (opposed to denial) was Commissioner Jim Renninger.
documentName: Board of County Commissioners Meeting Minutes, June 24, 2025 (Item 20)
extract: This is exactly the kind of secondary-source error the evidence ledger exists to catch: CitizenPortal.ai's specific commissioner-attribution claim is disproven by the primary minutes, even though its surrounding topline facts (date, acreage, 4-1 outcome) held up. Notably, Kristen Burke's actual role — she personally made the motion to deny, over staff/CAC/Planning-Commission recommendations of approval — is a stronger, better-documented fact than the garbled secondary-source version ever claimed. This is recorded neutrally: making a motion to deny a discretionary land-use application is a normal exercise of a commissioner's role and is not, by itself, evidence of any impropriety.

claim: Parcel 16-06-26-015574-001-02 (2005 S County Road 16, Green Cove Springs) has been homesteaded by owner Sheryl Edlyn Gustafson since 2013. Title passed through three same-day/adjacent $100 'Unqualified' family/trust transfers in December 2012: G Bar Ranch LLC → Gustafson Edwin S Jr, Trustee → Gustafson Edwin S Jr → Gustafson Sheryl Edlyn. 2026 TRIM just market value is $570,897; taxable value is $45,678 after homestead/Save Our Homes caps.
documentName: Clay County Property Appraiser — Parcel Report 16-06-26-015574-001-02
extract: Directly fetched the official Clay County Property Appraiser (qPublic) parcel report. All three 2012 transfers are coded 'Unqualified — UNQUAL/CORRECTIVE/QCD,TD' at nominal $100 consideration — standard for a family/trust reorganization, not an arm's-length market sale. This significantly changes the framing of the June 2025 land-use request: Sheryl Gustafson is a long-tenured homesteaded resident owner (13 years) exploring subdividing/selling her own property, not an outside developer who recently acquired land ahead of a rezoning vote. No sale in this record shows a market-rate transaction for this parcel. G Bar Ranch LLC / a similarly-named 'G Bar Ranch South, LLC' (Sunbiz, Green Cove Springs) appears to be a Gustafson-family ranching entity — not independently confirmed as identical to the 2012 grantor, flagged for follow-up (see RECORDS_NEEDED.md).
